quote: Bestimmung der Klassenanzahl für den Zahlkörper $x^3 - a = 0$ muss auf ellipti- sche Functionen mit dem Modul $\sqrt{-3}$ führen.
english: Determination of the class number for the number field $x^3 - a = 0$ must lead to elliptic functions with modulus $\sqrt{-3}$.
topic: A list of research problems: proving Dirichlet's habilitation theorems with ideal theory, representing integers as a square plus a cube via discriminants of cubic fields and complex multiplication, solving trinomial equations with modular functions, the class number of pure cubic fields, and a question about composing quadratic fields.

triage.modern_statement: For a cube-free integer a, let K = Q(∛a). Find an analytic class number formula for h_K, with the regulator log ε, that can be evaluated through elliptic or modular functions with complex multiplication by Q(√-3) (the 'modulus √-3'). The idea behind this: the Galois closure is K(ζ_3) = Q(√-3, ∛a), a cubic Kummer extension of Q(√-3). So ζ_K(s)/ζ(s) equals a Hecke L-function of a cubic character over Q(√-3). Its value at s=1, which gives h_K·log ε, should then be expressible through values of elliptic, eta or theta functions at points of Q(√-3), using a Kronecker limit formula.
triage.answered_by: Richard Dedekind, 'Ueber die Anzahl der Idealklassen in reinen kubischen Zahlkörpern', J. Reine Angew. Math. (Crelle) 121 (1900), 40–123. Dedekind wrote this landmark paper on the class number of pure cubic fields shortly after Hilbert's period of interest. My recollection, not confirmed by the sources I retrieved, is that Dedekind evaluated the relevant L-series over Q(√-3) with Kronecker's limit formula, i.e. with elliptic/modular functions attached to √-3. Later Kronecker-limit-formula analogues for cubic fields include Bump–Goldfeld (1984) and Bergeron–Charollois–García (complex cubic fields).

evidence.claim: Dedekind published 'Ueber die Anzahl der Idealklassen in reinen kubischen Zahlkörpern', J. Reine Angew. Math. 121 (1900), 40–123. It is the standard reference for class numbers of pure cubic fields.
Dedekind's 1900 Crelle paper on class numbers of pure cubic fields is listed as a reference on the problems of Galois theory. He also wrote a follow-up on units in pure cubic fields (1923 listing).
Kronecker-limit-type formulas for cubic fields are still being developed: Bump–Goldfeld 'A Kronecker limit formula for cubic fields' (1984).
Recent work builds elliptic-unit and Kronecker-limit analogues for complex cubic fields ('Eisenstein's Jugendtraum').
Class groups of pure cubic fields, e.g. 3-class groups of Q(∛p), are still being studied today.

triage.why: The note is a clear research programme: analytic class number of Q(∛a) via complex multiplication by Q(√-3). It is not one of Hilbert's 23 published problems. It was carried out essentially by Dedekind's 1900 Crelle memoir. The sources I found confirm the bibliographic facts of that memoir. They do not confirm my recollection that Dedekind's method is Kronecker's limit formula and eta/elliptic functions for Q(√-3); a search budget limit kept me from checking that directly, so confidence is medium. Kronecker limit formulas for cubic fields and class groups of pure cubic fields are still active topics.
